subject.title: refactor: delete dead infra and config exports

question: After the two gateway-lock regressions are repaired and the branch is cleanly rebased, is the remaining broad removal of internal exports and associated test coverage acceptable as one cleanup change?
rationale: The lock defects are mechanical, but accepting the resulting broad internal-contract and coverage reduction requires owner judgment under the protected maintainer label.

options.title: Repair and review the full cleanup
options.body: Restore the documented lock semantics, rebase, rerun exact-head broad validation, and review the remaining deletion set as one change.

options.title: Split the risky runtime changes
options.body: Keep the dead-export baseline cleanup separate and move gateway-lock or lifecycle behavior changes into narrowly proven follow-up pull requests.

options.title: Pause the broad cleanup
options.body: Close or substantially narrow the branch if the review and validation cost outweighs the current dead-export reduction.

recommendation.title: Repair and review the full cleanup
recommendation.body: Restore the documented lock semantics, rebase, rerun exact-head broad validation, and review the remaining deletion set as one change.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is the merged export-ratchet work that established this cleanup boundary.
